title: Organize and find items with labels
summary: Label related items and find them across the boards you can access.
benefit: Keep references and open questions easy to find without moving them out of context.
outcome: References share a reusable label, and a search takes you to a matching item even inside a collapsed column.
prerequisites: Edit access to a board to create or change labels; view access is enough to read labels and search accessible content.

sections.title: Use one label for related items
paragraphs: Labels add a small coloured name to an item. For example, label reference material Lighting and unresolved notes Question, then use Fetch to find matching items across boards.
A label belongs to its board. Reusing it on that board keeps its identity: renaming or recolouring it updates every use there. Labels with the same name on different boards are independent.
Label names can contain up to 80 characters. Long names wrap on the item rather than covering nearby content.

figures.alt: A narrow reference card shows Lighting, Question and seven additional labels wrapped inside its width.
figures.caption: Long names and several labels wrap within the item.

flow.entry: Select an item on an editable board. If a note is being edited, finish the edit with Escape first. On a phone, tap an item once to select it.

steps.action: Choose Labels in the selection toolbar.
steps.result: The label dialog lists this board's labels and shows how many items are selected.

steps.action: Enter a name such as Lighting, choose a colour if you want, and choose Create.
steps.result: The new label is applied to the selected item. Its chip appears on the item and its checkbox is selected in the dialog.

steps.action: Choose Done to return to the selection. On a phone, choose the selection sheet's Done button when you want the main navigation again.
steps.result: The label stays visible on the item, and you can continue working on the board.

flow.completion: Committed label changes save with the board and sync to your other signed-in sessions.
flow.correction: Undo reverses the most recent change; Redo restores it. If a label name already exists on this board, reuse its checkbox instead of creating another copy.

figures.alt: The Labels dialog shows shared usage counts, selected labels and guidance to reuse an existing name.
figures.caption: Reuse a name from the list when the dialog reports that it already exists.

sections.title: Reuse a label on several items

flow.entry: Select another item, or select several items together. Shift-click changes a desktop selection; on touch, use Select in the selection toolbar.

steps.action: Open Labels and select the checkbox beside an existing label.
steps.result: The same label is applied to every selected item. A partially selected checkbox means only some selected items currently use it.

steps.action: Clear a selected label's checkbox when you want to remove it from the selected items.
steps.result: Those items lose the label. Its definition remains available for reuse on this board.

flow.completion: The number beside each label counts its live uses on this board, including items inside collapsed columns. Trashed items do not count.
flow.correction: Undo restores the previous assignments for the selection in one step.

figures.alt: Two selected notes share Lighting and Question labels, with the Labels control in the selection toolbar.
figures.caption: Open Labels with several items selected to update their assignments together.

sections.title: Find a labelled item across boards

flow.entry: Open Fetch from the search button, or press Command-K on a Mac or Control-K on a PC.

steps.action: Type Lighting, or another label name.
steps.result: Matches show real item text or a description, the containing board, and any matching label. Fetch also searches board titles and item text.

steps.action: Choose a result, or use the arrow keys and Enter.
steps.result: DoggyNote opens the item's board, selects the item, and centres it. A collapsed column expands to reveal its matching member.

flow.completion: Search includes content you can access across boards. An unused label definition does not appear as an item result.
flow.correction: Escape closes Fetch without navigating. If an item becomes unavailable or access cannot be checked, retry the search instead of assuming the jump succeeded.

callout.title: Exploring a view-only board
callout.text: You can reveal a matching item without editing the board. View-only column expansion is local to the session; editable-board expansion is saved and can be undone.

figures.alt: Fetch shows two real notes returned by a Lighting label search, with their containing board context.
figures.caption: Search results keep the matching item text and its board context together.

sections.title: Rename, recolour or remove a label

flow.entry: Select an item and open Labels on the board whose labels you want to change.

steps.action: Choose Rename beside Lighting, enter Lighting references, and choose Save name.
steps.result: Every use of that label on this board shows the new name, and Fetch uses it for matching. Independent labels on other boards keep their own names.

steps.action: Choose a different colour from the menu beside the label.
steps.result: Every use on this board updates its colour without changing the assignments.

steps.action: Choose Remove beside a label when you want to remove it from the whole board.
steps.result: Its chips disappear from all items on the board. Clearing a checkbox instead removes it only from the selected items.

flow.completion: The saved name and colour are shared by this label's uses on its board.
flow.correction: Undo restores a removed label and its previous uses. Redo reapplies the removal. While renaming, Cancel or Escape abandons the unfinished name without changing the saved label.

sections.title: Saving and access
paragraphs: Saved labels return when you reopen the board or app. View-only users can read labels but cannot change their names, colours or assignments.

Label metadata, usage counts and search results follow board access. Private Inbox content stays private. When the app learns that access was removed, inaccessible search results disappear; an online jump checks access again.
Moving an item to another board reuses a destination label with the same name or creates an independent destination label. Other boards' labels are not renamed by that move.
